    79	/-- The four-register state on `AA'BA''`, obtained from the original state and
    80	the EPR pair on `A'A''` by the explicit four-factor shuffle. This is a Lean-only
    81	restriction of `eq:def-psihat` to its first register partition. -/
    82	noncomputable def psiHatAlicePair (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) :
    83	    EuclideanSpace ℂ (S.ExpandedLocalSpace .alice × S.ExpandedLocalSpace .bob) :=
    84	  reindexState prodShuffle (vecTensor S.toStrategy.ψ (eprState (PauliRegister P)))
    85	
    86	/-- The four-register state on `BB'AB''`. The original state is explicitly
    87	reversed from `AB` to `BA` before adjoining the EPR pair on `B'B''`; no symmetry
    88	of the strategy is used. This is a Lean-only restriction of `eq:def-psihat` to
    89	its second register partition. -/
    90	noncomputable def psiHatBobPair (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) :
    91	    EuclideanSpace ℂ (S.ExpandedLocalSpace .bob × S.ExpandedLocalSpace .alice) :=
    92	  reindexState prodShuffle
    93	    (vecTensor (reindexState (Equiv.prodComm _ _) S.toStrategy.ψ)
    94	      (eprState (PauliRegister P)))
    95	
    96	/-- Put `AA'BA''` and the unused pair `B'B''` into the six-register order of
    97	`eq:def-psihat`. This is an explicit coordinate permutation. -/
    98	def aliceSpectatorShuffle (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) :
    99	    ((S.ExpandedLocalSpace .alice × S.ExpandedLocalSpace .bob) ×
   100	        (PauliRegister P × PauliRegister P)) ≃
   101	      SixReg P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB where
   102	  toFun p := ((p.1.1.1, (p.1.1.2, p.1.2.2)), (p.1.2.1, p.2))
   103	  invFun p := (((p.1.1, p.1.2.1), (p.2.1, p.1.2.2)), p.2.2)
   104	  left_inv p := by cases p; rfl
   105	  right_inv p := by cases p; rfl
   106	
   107	/-- Put `BB'AB''` and the unused pair `A'A''` into the six-register order of
   108	`eq:def-psihat`. The permutation retains distinct original player spaces. -/
   109	def bobSpectatorShuffle (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) :
   110	    ((S.ExpandedLocalSpace .bob × S.ExpandedLocalSpace .alice) ×
   111	        (PauliRegister P × PauliRegister P)) ≃
   112	      SixReg P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB where
   113	  toFun p := ((p.1.2.1, p.2), (p.1.1.1, (p.1.1.2, p.1.2.2)))
   114	  invFun p := (((p.2.1, p.2.2.1), (p.1.1, p.2.2.2)), p.1.2)
   115	  left_inv p := by cases p; rfl
   116	  right_inv p := by cases p; rfl
   117	
   118	/-- Coordinate factorization of `eq:def-psihat` with the unused pair `B'B''`
   119	last. The remaining pair is exactly the one used by `AA'`, `BA''`. -/
   120	theorem psiHat_eq_alicePair_tensor_epr (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) :
   121	    S.psiHat = reindexState S.aliceSpectatorShuffle
   122	      (vecTensor S.psiHatAlicePair (eprState (PauliRegister P))) := by
   123	  ext p
   124	  rfl
   125	
   126	/-- Coordinate factorization of `eq:def-psihat` with the unused pair `A'A''`
   127	last. The remaining pair is exactly the one used by `BB'`, `AB''`. -/
   128	theorem psiHat_eq_bobPair_tensor_epr (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) :
   129	    S.psiHat = reindexState S.bobSpectatorShuffle
   130	      (vecTensor S.psiHatBobPair (eprState (PauliRegister P))) := by
   131	  ext p
   132	  change (S.toStrategy.ψ (p.1.1, p.2.1) *
   133	      eprState (PauliRegister P) p.1.2) * eprState (PauliRegister P) p.2.2 =
   134	    (S.toStrategy.ψ (p.1.1, p.2.1) *
   135	      eprState (PauliRegister P) p.2.2) * eprState (PauliRegister P) p.1.2
   136	  exact mul_right_comm _ _ _
   137	
   138	/-- Arbitrary operators on `AA'` and `BA''` multiply to their tensor product,
   139	with the identity on `B'B''`, in the coordinates of `eq:def-psihat`. -/
   140	theorem place_AA'_mul_BA'' (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
   141	    (A : Op (S.ExpandedLocalSpace .alice)) (B : Op (S.ExpandedLocalSpace .bob)) :
   142	    S.place .AA' A * S.place .BA'' B =
   143	      reindexOp S.aliceSpectatorShuffle.symm
   144	        (heteroKron (heteroKron A B) (1 : Op (PauliRegister P × PauliRegister P))) := by
   145	  classical
   146	  ext i j
   147	  simp [Matrix.mul_apply, Fintype.sum_prod_type, place, reindexOp, heteroKron,
   148	    aliceSpectatorShuffle, Matrix.one_apply, mul_ite, ite_mul, Prod.ext_iff,
   149	    ite_and]
   150	  split_ifs <;> rfl
   151	
   152	/-- Arbitrary operators on `BB'` and `AB''` multiply to their tensor product,
   153	with the identity on `A'A''`, in the coordinates of `eq:def-psihat`. -/
   154	theorem place_BB'_mul_AB'' (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
   155	    (B : Op (S.ExpandedLocalSpace .bob)) (A : Op (S.ExpandedLocalSpace .alice)) :
   156	    S.place .BB' B * S.place .AB'' A =
   157	      reindexOp S.bobSpectatorShuffle.symm
   158	        (heteroKron (heteroKron B A) (1 : Op (PauliRegister P × PauliRegister P))) := by
   159	  classical
   160	  ext i j
   161	  simp [Matrix.mul_apply, Fintype.sum_prod_type, place, reindexOp, heteroKron,
   162	    bobSpectatorShuffle, Matrix.one_apply, mul_ite, ite_mul, mul_comm, Prod.ext_iff,
   163	    ite_and]
   164	  rfl
   165	
   166	/-- Removing the unused pair `B'B''` preserves the complex expectation of an
   167	arbitrary product on `AA'`, `BA''`. The four-register state retains the EPR pair
   168	on `A'A''`. This is a Lean-only exact identity for `eq:def-psihat`, requiring
   169	neither positivity of the operators nor symmetry of the strategy. -/
   170	theorem psiHat_expectation_AA'_BA'' (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
   171	    (A : Op (S.ExpandedLocalSpace .alice)) (B : Op (S.ExpandedLocalSpace .bob)) :
   172	    inner ℂ S.psiHat (applyOperatorToState (S.place .AA' A * S.place .BA'' B) S.psiHat) =
   173	      inner ℂ S.psiHatAlicePair
   174	        (applyOperatorToState (heteroKron A B) S.psiHatAlicePair) := by
   175	  rw [place_AA'_mul_BA'', psiHat_eq_alicePair_tensor_epr]
   176	  exact inner_reindex_tensor_epr_one S.aliceSpectatorShuffle S.psiHatAlicePair (heteroKron A B)
   177	
   178	/-- Removing the unused pair `A'A''` preserves the complex expectation of an
   179	arbitrary product on `BB'`, `AB''`. The remaining state uses the original
   180	strategy with explicitly reversed coordinates and the EPR pair on `B'B''`.
   181	This is the second Lean-only spectator identity for `eq:def-psihat`. -/
   182	theorem psiHat_expectation_BB'_AB'' (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
   183	    (B : Op (S.ExpandedLocalSpace .bob)) (A : Op (S.ExpandedLocalSpace .alice)) :
   184	    inner ℂ S.psiHat (applyOperatorToState (S.place .BB' B * S.place .AB'' A) S.psiHat) =
   185	      inner ℂ S.psiHatBobPair
   186	        (applyOperatorToState (heteroKron B A) S.psiHatBobPair) := by
   187	  rw [place_BB'_mul_AB'', psiHat_eq_bobPair_tensor_epr]
   188	  exact inner_reindex_tensor_epr_one S.bobSpectatorShuffle S.psiHatBobPair (heteroKron B A)
   189	
   190	end ProjectiveSetting
   191	
   192	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

    83	/--
    84	The tensor-product strategy of blueprint
    85	`def:tensor-product-strategy` (paper origin
    86	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:26-38`).
    87	-/
    88	structure Strategy (G : Game) where
    89	  ιA : Type
    90	  ιB : Type
    91	  [ιAFintype : Fintype ιA]
    92	  [ιBFintype : Fintype ιB]
    93	  [ιADecidableEq : DecidableEq ιA]
    94	  [ιBDecidableEq : DecidableEq ιB]
    95	  ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA × ιB)
    96	  ψ_norm : ‖ψ‖ = 1
    97	  A : G.QuestionA → Measurement G.AnswerA ιA
    98	  B : G.QuestionB → Measurement G.AnswerB ιB
    99	
   100	attribute [instance] Strategy.ιAFintype Strategy.ιBFintype
   101	  Strategy.ιADecidableEq Strategy.ιBDecidableEq
   102	
   103	/-- The rectangular tensor placement used in strategy probabilities.  This is
   104	the finite-matrix realization of blueprint
   105	`def:tensor-product-strategy`; paper origin
   106	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:26-38`.
   107	-/
   108	def heteroKron {ιA ιB : Type*} (A : Op ιA) (B : Op ιB) : Op (ιA × ιB) :=
   109	  Matrix.kronecker A B
   110	
   111	/-! ### Algebra of the tensor placement
   112	
   113	The shared tensor-placement API.  These identities are used both by the perfect
   114	Magic Square strategy (blueprint `thm:ms-from-ac`) and by the rigidity transfer
   115	step (blueprint `thm:ms-rigidity`), so they live
   116	with the definition rather than in either development. -/
   117	
   118	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for `def:tensor-product-strategy`
   119	(blueprint `def:tensor-product-strategy`, paper
   120	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:26-38`): the tensor
   121	placement is multiplicative, `(A ⊗ C) * (B ⊗ D) = (A * B) ⊗ (C * D)`. -/
   122	theorem heteroKron_mul {ιA ιB : Type*} [Fintype ιA] [Fintype ιB]
   123	    (A B : Op ιA) (C D : Op ιB) :
   124	    heteroKron A C * heteroKron B D = heteroKron (A * B) (C * D) := by
   125	  unfold heteroKron Matrix.kronecker
   126	  exact (Matrix.mul_kronecker_mul A B C D).symm
   127	
   128	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for `def:tensor-product-strategy`
   129	(blueprint `def:tensor-product-strategy`): the tensor
   130	placement of the two identity operators is the identity operator on the product
   131	space. -/
   132	theorem heteroKron_one_one {ιA ιB : Type*} [DecidableEq ιA] [DecidableEq ιB] :
   133	    heteroKron (1 : Op ιA) (1 : Op ιB) = 1 := by
   134	  unfold heteroKron Matrix.kronecker
   135	  exact Matrix.one_kronecker_one
   136	
   137	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for `def:tensor-product-strategy`
   138	(blueprint `def:tensor-product-strategy`): tensor placement
   139	respects negation in the left factor. -/
   140	theorem heteroKron_neg_left {ιA ιB : Type*} (A : Op ιA) (C : Op ιB) :
   141	    heteroKron (-A) C = -heteroKron A C := by
   142	  ext p q
   143	  simp [heteroKron, Matrix.kronecker]
   144	
   145	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for `def:tensor-product-strategy`
   146	(blueprint `def:tensor-product-strategy`): tensor placement
   147	respects negation in the right factor. -/
   148	theorem heteroKron_neg_right {ιA ιB : Type*} (A : Op ιA) (C : Op ιB) :
   149	    heteroKron A (-C) = -heteroKron A C := by
   150	  ext p q
   151	  simp [heteroKron, Matrix.kronecker]
   152	
   153	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for `def:tensor-product-strategy`
   154	(blueprint `def:tensor-product-strategy`): tensor placement
   155	is additive in the left factor. -/
   156	theorem heteroKron_add_left {ιA ιB : Type*} (A B : Op ιA) (C : Op ιB) :
   157	    heteroKron (A + B) C = heteroKron A C + heteroKron B C := by
   158	  ext p q
   159	  simp [heteroKron, Matrix.kronecker, add_mul]
   160	
   161	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for `def:tensor-product-strategy`
   162	(blueprint `def:tensor-product-strategy`): tensor placement
   163	is additive in the right factor. -/
   164	theorem heteroKron_add_right {ιA ιB : Type*} (A : Op ιA) (B C : Op ιB) :
   165	    heteroKron A (B + C) = heteroKron A B + heteroKron A C := by
   166	  ext p q
   167	  simp [heteroKron, Matrix.kronecker, mul_add]
   168	
   169	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for `def:tensor-product-strategy`: the
   170	tensor placement of possibly rectangular matrices respects differences in the
   171	left factor.  This is the general form of `heteroKron_sub_left` below, needed
   172	where the left factor is the matrix of an isometry between distinct index
   173	types (blueprint
   174	`thm:ms-rigidity`). -/
   175	theorem kroneckerMap_sub_left {m n p q : Type*} (A B : Matrix m n ℂ) (C : Matrix p q ℂ) :
   176	    Matrix.kroneckerMap (· * ·) (A - B) C =
   177	      Matrix.kroneckerMap (· * ·) A C - Matrix.kroneckerMap (· * ·) B C := by
   178	  ext p' q'
   179	  simp [Matrix.kroneckerMap, sub_mul]
   180	
   181	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for `def:tensor-product-strategy`: the
   182	tensor placement of possibly rectangular matrices respects differences in the
   183	right factor.  This is the general form of `heteroKron_sub_right` below. -/
   184	theorem kroneckerMap_sub_right {m n p q : Type*} (A : Matrix m n ℂ) (B C : Matrix p q ℂ) :
   185	    Matrix.kroneckerMap (· * ·) A (B - C) =
   186	      Matrix.kroneckerMap (· * ·) A B - Matrix.kroneckerMap (· * ·) A C := by
   187	  ext p' q'
   188	  simp [Matrix.kroneckerMap, mul_sub]
   189	
   190	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for `def:tensor-product-strategy`

    18	\section{At a glance}
    19	
    20	\begin{itemize}
    21	  \item \textbf{Difficulty: medium.}  Two related matters are recorded.
    22	  First, the soundness analysis of the Pauli basis test invokes the
    23	  classical low individual degree game at dimension $2m+2$, and the game's
    24	  question distribution is undefined at that dimension for the admissible
    25	  parameters: it requires $2m+2$ to divide $q$, while admissibility supplies
    26	  only $m \mid q$. The directly indexed reformulation and its soundness
    27	  proof are established for $k=1$; their use in the combining subtree
    28	  remains to be verified. Second, the source's import of the classical
    29	  game's quantum soundness from the tensor-code paper carries two open
    30	  verification obligations at every dimension: the asserted identity with
    31	  the cited tensor-code test is not an identity and must be replaced by a
    32	  reduction with a value bound, and the source's instantiation of the
    33	  theorem's auxiliary parameter violates its lower bound at small
    34	  dimensions (Section~\ref{sec:import-obligations}).

    36	  value-preserving correlated-register dilation, and the compression
    37	  argument are proved. They yield all three soundness conclusions with
    38	  error $\delta_{\mathrm{ld}}$ for $k=1$. The proof applies the low
    39	  individual degree theorem directly and avoids the two obligations of
    40	  the printed tensor-code import. The arbitrary-$k$ combining reduction
    41	  and the downstream use at dimension $2m+2$ remain open.

    51	  \item \textbf{Key Mathlib inputs:} uniform distributions on finite types
    52	  and their maps, and elementary divisibility arithmetic on powers of two.

    58	\section{Key theorem forms}
    59	
    60	Throughout, $q = 2^k$ with $k$ odd is an admissible field size, the tuple
    61	$(q,m,d)$ is admissible when moreover $d \ge 1$ and $m \mid q$, and
    62	$\mathrm{ideg}_{d,m}(\F_q)$ denotes the $m$-variate polynomial representatives
    63	over $\F_q$ of individual degree at most $d$.  The comparison involves four
    64	theorem forms.
    65	\begin{enumerate}
    66	  \item \textbf{Source theorem form} (the polynomial-pair measurement).  There
    67	  is a function $\delta_S(\eps,m,d,q) = a(md)^a(\eps^b + q^{-b} + 2^{-bmd})$,
    68	  for universal constants $a > 1$ and $0 < b < 1$, such that for every
    69	  admissible $(q,m,d)$ and every projective strategy for the Pauli basis test
    70	  succeeding with probability at least $1-\eps$, there is a projective
    71	  measurement $\{\hat S_{g_X,g_Z}\}$ with outcomes pairs of polynomials in
    72	  $\mathrm{ideg}_{d,m}(\F_q)$ whose evaluations are $\delta_S$-consistent, on
    73	  average over a uniform point $u \in \F_q^m$ and in both bases
    74	  $W \in \{X,Z\}$, with the corresponding points measurements
    75	  $\{\hat M^{(\mathrm{Point},W),u}_a\}$ of the strategy, together with the
    76	  symmetric counterpart of this relation.
    77	  \item \textbf{Missing instantiation obligation.}  The classical low
    78	  individual degree game with parameter tuple $(q,\, 2m+2,\, d,\, 1)$ is well
    79	  defined, and the combined point and line measurements assembled in the
    80	  analysis constitute a strategy for it of value at least
    81	  $1 - \delta_{\mathrm{combine}}$.  The game's question distribution draws
    82	  its axis and diagonal indices through an index function
    83	  $\chi_{2m+2}\colon \F_q \to \{1,\ldots,2m+2\}$ with classes of equal size
    84	  $q/(2m+2)$, so the game exists only when $2m+2$ divides $q$.
    85	  \item \textbf{Restricted form supported by the present route.}  The source
    86	  theorem form under the additional hypothesis $2m+2 \mid q$.  Among
    87	  admissible tuples this hypothesis holds exactly when $m = 1$ and
    88	  $q \ge 8$; it fails for every admissible tuple with $m \ge 2$ and for
    89	  $(q,m) = (2,1)$.
    90	  \item \textbf{Repaired import form} (recommended target).  Quantum
    91	  soundness of the directly indexed variant of the classical low individual
    92	  degree game over $\F_q^{m'}$, for every dimension $m' \ge 1$ and
    93	  admissible $q$, with no divisibility hypothesis: the question
    94	  distribution samples the axis index, and the diagonal prefix index,
    95	  uniformly from $\{1,\ldots,m'\}$ directly rather than through an index
    96	  function on $\F_q$, and line questions carry the sampled index itself in
    97	  place of the seed $s \in \F_q$; the error is
    98	  $\delta_{\mathrm{ld}}(\eps,q,m',d,k) = a(dm'k)^a(\eps^b + q^{-b} +
    99	  2^{-bm'd})$. This form is proved for $k=1$, as is its transport to the
   100	  seed-indexed game when $m'\mid q$. The proof uses the low individual
   101	  degree theorem directly, rather than the tensor-code import of
   102	  Section~\ref{sec:import-obligations}. Only the extension to arbitrary
   103	  $k$ remains open in this soundness assertion.
   104	\end{enumerate}

   106	\section{The source assertion and the obstruction}
   107	
   108	We examine the final step of the subsection ``Applying the classical
   109	low-degree test'' in the analysis of the Pauli basis test in the compression
   110	paper of Ji, Natarajan, Vidick, Wright, and Yuen (MIP$^{*}$=RE,
   111	arXiv:2001.04383), whose quantum soundness component builds on the low
   112	individual degree test of \cite{Ji2020LowIndividualDegree}.%
   113	\footnote{Tracked in \localissue{0002}.  In the mirror of the source
   114	consulted here, the polynomial-pair lemma and its proof are at
   115	\path{references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex},
   116	lines~1267--1288; the sub-line lemma is at lines~1063--1116 and the combined
   117	line lemma at lines~1020--1034 of the same file.  The game parametrization
   118	with its divisibility, the index function, the soundness statement with its
   119	proof, and admissibility are at
   120	\path{references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex},
   121	lines~33--35, 214--219, 413--458, and 958--961.}
   122	There, the combined point measurements
   123	$\{\hat Q^{x,z,\alpha,\beta}_c\}$ and combined line measurements
   124	$\{\hat Q^{\ell}_f\}$, indexed by points of $\F_q^{2m+2}$ and lines in
   125	$\F_q^{2m+2}$, are asserted to form a strategy for the classical low
   126	individual degree game with parameters
   127	\[
   128	  \mathsf{ldparams} = (q,\, 2m+2,\, d,\, 1)
   129	  \tag{\path{lem:qld-4-7}}
   130	\]
   131	of value $1 - \delta_{\mathrm{combine}}$, and the quantum soundness theorem
   132	for that game is applied to produce the global polynomial-pair measurement.
   133	The two lemmas feeding this step are stated for the line-point distribution
   134	over $\F_q^{2m+2}$.
   135	
   136	The game, however, is parametrized by tuples $(q,m',d,k)$ with $q$ an
   137	admissible field size \emph{and $m'$ dividing $q$}.  The divisibility is not
   138	incidental: the question distribution is a conditionally linear distribution
   139	in which a uniform seed coordinate $s \in \F_q$, read as an integer in
   140	$\{0,\ldots,q-1\}$, determines the axis or diagonal index through the unique
   141	$\chi(s)$ with
   142	\[
   143	  s = (\chi(s)-1)\,\frac{q}{m'} + r, \qquad 0 \le r < \frac{q}{m'},
   144	  \tag{\path{eq:chi-func}}
   145	\]
